listed_for_build_unverified.name: CO2 laser tube power disputed
listed_for_build_unverified.source_line: A responder disputes the tube's stated power based on its visible/estimated length and challenges the axis-rod size and direct stepper drive arrangement. The builder accepts that the Y drive shafts and transmission should be revisited and mentions possible Panasonic servo motors. Other participants disagree with the responder's tube-power inference and discuss tube length/output variability. Therefore, tube identity and power are **contested/unknown**, not settled as 40 W, 80 W, or 100 W.

exclusions.name: LightObject DSP planned only
exclusions.reason: Existing or proposed controller belongs to the replaced control system, not the machine periphery.
exclusions.source_line: The builder calls this a second laser-cutter attempt, after building an early Buildlog.net design. The author reports about one month of design/build time and an estimated £1,500–£2,000 cost. At the thread's opening, the builder describes it as a 40 W machine and says a LightObject DSP would control the laser and steppers; upgrading to 80 W or 100 W was only a possibility.
